definitions.explanation: What is left of something after it has been destroyed — a burned-out car, a crashed plane, a collapsed building. The word keeps the shape of the original object in view, so it suggests a recognizable wreck rather than formless debris.

examples.japanese: ⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{残骸|ざんがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}っていた→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: The wreckage of a car was left there.
After the fire, the house stood there as a burned-out shell.

examples.japanese: ⟦{墜落|ついらく}した→墜落する：21423_tsuirakusuru⟧⟦{飛行機|ひこうき}→飛行機：00629_hikouki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{残骸|ざんがい}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{調|しら}べられている→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧。
examples.english: The cause of the accident is being investigated from the wreckage of the crashed plane.

notes:
Also used figuratively for what survives of something abstract that has broken down, as in ⟦{帝国|ていこく}→帝国：12420_teikoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{残骸|ざんがい} (the remnants of an empire).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {残骸|ざんがい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧: wreckage remains
- {残骸|ざんがい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{片付|かたづ}ける→片付ける：01192_katazukeru⟧: to clear away the wreckage
- ⟦{船|ふね}→船：00775_fune⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{残骸|ざんがい}: the wreck of a ship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{瓦礫|がれき}→瓦礫：30524_gareki⟧: rubble — broken pieces with no recognizable shape left
- ⟦{廃墟|はいきょ}→廃墟：12453_haikyo⟧: ruins — a whole abandoned building or site, often long derelict
